paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. The master commended the manager because he acted shrewdly (Luke 16:8). The manager saw trouble coming, and he used what was in his hands right then to get ready for what came next. Jesus says, "the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light" (Luke 16:8), and I think He's asking us to put that same hustle toward things that last.

So what's the plan? Jesus says, "use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings" (Luke 16:9). Paychecks, bills and that stuff in your wallet won't last, but what you do with it can point past today. And He says, "Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much" (Luke 16:10), so the small stuff counts. One honest cookie today shows what you'll do with the whole cookie box.

Then comes the line that holds it all together: "You cannot serve both God and money" (Luke 16:13). Money is a fine tool and a terrible boss. So ask yourself, baker, who is the one running your oven timer? Pick the right Master, be faithful with what He puts in your hands, and then LET'S GO BAKE.
